key_insight: For linear elastostatics, minimizing discrete potential energy is exactly supervised regression in the energy norm, aligning surrogate training with stress accuracy rather than displacement accuracy.
engineering_relevance: Energy-norm training improves stress predictions for perforated plates and solids with cavities, where holes concentrate stress.
method: Train and evaluate finite-element surrogates using the energy norm.
Train without solution labels by minimizing assembled discrete potential energy.
Screen predictions within a load case using energy; its sign flags predictions worse than the zero field.
evidence_signal: In pre-registered comparisons, changing only the supervised loss norm reduced a 3D transformer's median energy-norm error 7.5-fold and median von Mises error 6.1-fold; 2D von Mises error more than halved, including on held-out instances.
watch_item: No network transferred to a substantially finer mesh; when the stiffness matrix was available, Ritz projection outperformed the label-free transformer in seed means on every metric except peak stress.
paper_title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm
